q: 141. Softer variety of steel may e obtained by .....
explain: As per the answer key, the Bessemer process gives a softer (low carbon, mild) steel.

q: 142. The steel which contains fissures and cavities manufactured by .....
explain: Cementation produces blister steel, whose surface shows blisters, fissures and cavities caused by escaping gases.

q: 143. Cast steel is manufactured by .....
explain: Cast steel is made by the crucible process, melting steel or wrought iron with charcoal in crucibles.

q: 144. For high grade instruments the steel preferred to, is .....
explain: Cast steel is homogeneous, hard and takes a fine edge, so it is used for high grade instruments and tools.

q: 145. The steel used in R.C.C. work is .....
explain: Mild steel is ductile and weldable, so it is used as reinforcement in R.C.C.

q: 146. The most important constituent of varnish, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option d. Note: resin is generally the key ingredient of varnish, so the key answer is debatable.

q: 147. Snowcrete is one of the patent forms of .....
explain: Snowcrete (like Snowcem) is a patented water-proof cement paint.

q: 148. The most fire resistant, paints are .....
explain: Asbestos paints are the most fire resistant since asbestos does not burn.

q: 149. To give a brilliant finish the type of varnish used, is .....
explain: Spirit varnish dries quickly and gives a brilliant, glossy finish.

q: 150. The most durable varnish is .....
explain: Oil varnish forms a tough, durable film and is the most durable type.

q: 151. Oilwell cement is generally used for .....
explain: Oil well cement is specially made to set properly at the high temperature and pressure found in oil wells.

q: 152. The fluxing agent in the manufacturing of white cement is .....
explain: Cryolite is used as the fluxing agent in white cement manufacture (printed 'gryolite'). Option d is blank in the book.

q: 153. The mass of cement present in a standard cement bag is .....
explain: A standard cement bag contains 50 kg of cement.

q: 154. In the manufacturing of cement the nodules form the rotary kiln are called .....
explain: The hard nodules that come out of the rotary kiln are called clinker.

q: 155. The glass used for security purpose is .....
explain: Bullet proof glass is used where security is required.

q: 156. Glazing of clay products, is done .....
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing improves appearance, makes the product impervious and protects it from weather and corrosive action.

q: 157. A pug mill is used for .....
explain: A pug mill is used for tempering (thoroughly mixing) brick earth with water.

q: 158. A badly mixed cement concrete results in .....
explain: As per the answer key, honeycombing. Poorly mixed concrete leaves voids, giving a honeycombed surface.

q: 159. For a 50 kg cement bag water required, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, 22.5 litres, which corresponds to a water-cement ratio of 0.45.

q: 160. Minimum required water cement ratio for a workable concrete is .....
explain: As per the answer key, 0.40 is the minimum water-cement ratio for workable concrete.

q: 161. Inner part of a timber log surrounding the pith is called .....
explain: The dark inner part around the pith is the heartwood.

q: 162. Age of tree may be ascertained by .....
explain: One ring forms per year, so the number of annual rings gives the age.

q: 163. Seasoning of timber is essential to remove .....
explain: Seasoning removes sap and moisture from timber to prevent decay and shrinkage.

q: 164. A piece of sawn timber whose cross-sectional dimensions exceed 5 cm, in one direction and ... cm in the other direction, is called a .....
explain: A baulk is a large sawn timber piece. Part of the question text is cut off in the scan, so the missing number is shown as '...' and I could not verify it. The answer key gives c.

q: 165. The main constituents which imparts hydraulicity to hydraulic lime is .....
explain: As per the answer key, clay (silica, alumina and iron oxide in clay) gives lime its hydraulicity.

q: 166. Apiece of timber whose thickness and width are respectively 5 cm and 10 cm is called .....
explain: As per the answer key, such a small section piece is called a strip.

q: 167. Seasoning of timber is done .....
explain: Seasoning removes water (sap and moisture) from timber.

q: 168. Based on its dry weight, a freshly felled tree may contain water.
explain: As per the answer key, a freshly felled tree may contain water up to about 100% of its dry weight.

q: 169. Bloating of bricks is due to .....
options: presence of excess carbonaceous matter in the clay
presence of gas forming material in the clay
explain: Bloating is caused by gases trapped in the brick, from carbonaceous matter, gas-forming materials or rapid burning.

q: 170. Swelling of bricks is known as .....
explain: The swelling of bricks during burning is called bloating.

q: 171. To which category do the chromite bricks belong?
explain: Chromite bricks are neutral refractory bricks, and so are bricks of bauxite and carbon.

q: 172. Which of the following cement contains maximum percentage of di-calcium silicate?
explain: Low heat cement has a high proportion of C2S, which hydrates slowly and liberates little heat.

q: 173. The lime which contains high percentage of calcium oxide, is generally called .....
explain: As per the answer key, fat lime, which is high in calcium oxide and slakes vigorously with a large increase in volume. 'Rich lime' also describes it, but the key gives a.

q: 174. The property by virtue of which lime sets under water, is known as .....
explain: Hydraulicity is the ability of lime to set and harden under water.

q: 175. For construction of structures under water, the type of lime used, is .....
explain: Hydraulic lime sets under water, so it is used for underwater work.

q: 176. Pozzolana (or surkhi) is used in lime .....
options: to decrease the cost of construction
explain: Pozzolana reacts with lime in the presence of water, giving it hydraulic properties.

q: 177. The specific gravity of stone should not, in any case, be less than .....
explain: As per the answer key, the specific gravity of a good building stone should not be less than 2.5.

q: 178. The colour of granite is .....
explain: Granite occurs in grey, green, brown, pink and other colours.

q: 179. Portland cement manufactured from pure white chalk and clay but free from iron oxide, is known as .....
explain: Cement made from white chalk and china clay, free from iron oxide, is white cement.

q: 180. In paints, pigment is responsible for .....
explain: Pigments give paint its colour.

q: 181. Vanadium steel is generally used for .....
explain: As per the answer key, vanadium steel is used for axles and springs because of its toughness and fatigue resistance.

q: 182. The type of steel used for precision leveling staff, is .....
explain: Invar has almost zero thermal expansion, so it is used for precision levelling staves and measuring tapes.

q: 183. Invar contains .....
explain: Invar is an iron-nickel alloy with about 36% nickel. The book prints 'nicked' and '30% to nickel' in options a and c.

q: 184. An assembled product made up of veneers and adhesives is called .....
explain: Plywood is made by gluing thin veneers together.

q: 185. The thickness of five-ply sheet varies from .....
explain: As per the answer key, five-ply sheets are 6 to 9 mm thick.

q: 186. The thickness of lamin boards vary from .....
explain: As per the answer key, laminboards are 12 to 25 mm thick.

q: 187. The wood generally used for railway sleepers is .....
explain: As per the answer key, kail is generally used for railway sleepers.

q: 188. The chief ingredient of a paint is .....
explain: Pigment is the chief ingredient, giving colour and body to the paint.

q: 189. The liquid medium used in oil paints is .....
explain: Linseed oil is the liquid medium (vehicle) of oil paints.

q: 190. The pigment in paints is mixed to give desired .....
explain: Pigment is added to give the desired colour.

q: 191. The liquid part of the paint is called .....
explain: The liquid part (usually oil) that carries the pigment is the vehicle.

q: 192. The liquid medium used in enamel paints is .....
explain: Enamel paint is made by mixing pigment (white lead or zinc white) in varnish.

q: 193. The metallic oxide used in the form of powder in a paint is called .....
explain: The base is a metallic oxide in powder form, such as white lead, zinc oxide or titanium white.

q: 194. The base in a paint is added to .....
options: hide the surface to be painted
explain: As per the answer key, the base gives the paint body and opacity so it hides the surface to be painted.

q: 195. The commonly base used in a paint is .....
explain: Any of these can be used as a paint base.

q: 196. The thinner used for oil paints is .....
explain: Turpentine is the usual thinner for oil paints; water does not mix with oil.

q: 197. Linseed oil in paint is used as a .....
explain: Linseed oil acts as the carrier of pigment and dries to form a film.

q: 198. Linseed oil is rapidly soluble in .....
explain: As per the answer key, all of these. Linseed oil is soluble in turpentine and naphtha, and the key accepts alcohol too.

q: 199. The commonly used extender in a paint is .....
explain: As per the answer key, any one of these. Barium sulphate and gypsum are extenders, and alcohol is included in the book's key answer.

q: 200. The drier in an oil paint should not be more than ..... (by volume).
explain: As per the answer key, driers should not exceed 10% by volume.

q: 201. The commonly used solvent in oil paints is .....
explain: Turpentine or naphtha can be used as the solvent.

q: 202. Galvanizing means covering iron with a thin coat of .....
explain: Galvanizing coats iron or steel with zinc to protect it from rust.

q: 203. For the manufacture of stainless steel, steel is mixed with .....
explain: As per the answer key, chromium (stainless steel also contains some nickel).

q: 204. The cement mortar mix commonly used for external plastering and plastering of reinforced cement concrete works is .....
explain: A rich 1:3 mix is used for external plastering and for plastering R.C.C. work.

q: 205. Pointing is the process whereby .....
options: the masonry joints are filled up with mortar after raking out for small depth
the grooves are cut on a plastered surface to give a look of masonry
small circles looking like points are cut out at random on a plastered surface
explain: In pointing, the joints are raked out to a small depth and filled with better mortar.

q: 206. The process of applying cement mortar under pressure through a nozzle is called .....
explain: Spraying cement mortar under pressure through a nozzle is guniting (shotcreting).

q: 207. Slump test facilitates .....
options: controlling of water-cement ratio of concrete during construction
the determination of initial and final setting times of cement
the determination of workability of concrete
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: the slump test is normally described as a test of workability (option c), and the key answer is debatable. It does help control water content on site.

q: 208. The concrete mix used for general R.C.C. work is .....
explain: A 1:2:4 (cement : sand : aggregate) mix is generally used for R.C.C.

q: 209. Which one of the following does not belong to endogenous trees .....
explain: Palm, bamboo and cane are endogenous (inward growing); teak is exogenous.

q: 210. Which one of the following does not belong to exogenous trees .....
explain: Shisham, teak and sal are exogenous; coconut is endogenous, so it is the one that does not belong. In the book the options are printed in the order a, c, b, d (coconut, teak, shisham, sal), and the key gives a, coconut.
